market_holds: Front-expiry (11-13) straddle implies a 7.04% move, ATM IV 119%, and the skew is inverted: 25-delta puts are 14.1 vol points cheaper than calls, so upside is the side being paid for (put/call OI 0.65). Sealed baseline, 2026-11-12 18:09 UTC. The tape: spot 390.92 at the seal and about 382.8 at 19:27 UTC (Yahoo 15-minute bars), fading into the print. +22.5% over 5 sessions off the 319.25 close on 11-05, -9.1% over 20 sessions, -46% from the 723 closing high of 2026-06-30, 20-day realised vol 86%. The fall from 542 (10-05) to 319 (11-05) went with the whole group: SOXX 196 to 132, LRCX 346 to 185, KLAC 207 to 130. Causes were an AI-capex scare, a weak 10-13 investor day (2030 margin targets but no revenue target, -7.2%), and the post-midterm rout on 11-05 (Nasdaq -5.5%, AMAT -13.6%) with no company news. Consensus for FQ4: revenue about $10.30bn and EPS $4.06 (Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 11-04), whisper $4.20. The guide is $10.25bn +/- $0.5bn and EPS $4.02 +/- $0.20. FY27 normalised EPS consensus is $18.56, up from $17.00 three months earlier (TIKR, 11-09), so estimates have been rising while the stock fell. No public FQ1 FY27 revenue consensus was findable. FQ1 is a 14-week quarter with a flagged opex step-up and a tax rate rising to about 13%. The stock trades on that FQ1 guide and the 2027 framing, not on FQ4 (TIKR, Finviz/EW). Sentiment on EW is 19.8% bullish, down from 25.1%. Forward P/E is about 21x after the 11-09 jump (49x on 06-30). B. Riley cut its target to $475 from $700 on 11-09, lowering the bar. Seven prior prints: 5 of 7 down, median |move| 5.25%, including -5.1% on a beat-and-raise in 2026-08.
view: The industry data since Applied last spoke is plainly strong. KLA (10-28) set 2027 WFE above $200bn, roughly +30%, guided December revenue +13.5% q/q, and rose about 5% the next day against a falling group. Tokyo Electron's first FY3/27 forecast is ¥3.7tn revenue. Samsung guided 2026 capex up about 60%. Lam (10-21) beat but guided December only about in line, with supply-chain limits on shipments, and fell 11.7% on a day the whole group fell 7-10%. Hyperscalers were mixed: Microsoft cut CY26 capex on third-party data-centre delays, while Alphabet and Amazon said 2027 spending rises significantly. So Applied will very likely print near or above the FQ4 midpoint and guide a large 14-week FQ1, and the demand evidence points up. But that evidence is public, and the consensus already follows it (FY27 EPS revised up 9% in three months). The stock's 46% fall is a multiple and narrative collapse (AI-capex fear, midterm policy risk), and one company's guide answers that only partly. The relief trade has also partly run: +22% in five sessions, call skew richer than puts, and a fade today. Against the upside sits the stock's habit of falling on good prints (5 of 7). Lam's in-line, supply-capped December guide and Applied's own flagged opex/tax step-up and flat gross margin could also make the EPS guide look light even if revenue is strong. Net: a mild upside lean from depressed positioning and strong peer read-through, not enough to bet on.

recommendation.reason: The peer read-through (KLA's 2027 WFE +30%, TEL's FY27 forecast, Samsung capex) points to a strong FQ1 guide. But it is public, and consensus has been revised up to meet it, so I cannot show a gap between the stale number and the likely guide. The price is driven by macro AI-capex sentiment that one guide resolves only partly. A 22% five-day bounce with upside skew already paid takes away much of the relief edge. Without an FQ1 consensus to measure against, the direction is closer to a coin than to 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An FQ1 revenue guide well above roughly $11bn with an explicit 2027 WFE or Applied-growth number at or above KLA's +30% framing would push p_up toward 65+. An EPS guide below about $4.20 on opex/tax, or supply-chain or China caveats like Lam's, would push it toward 35.

self_critique: The case for up is stronger than 55 might suggest. Every equipment peer that reported since Applied's August call confirmed demand accelerating into 2027. The stock sits at ~20x FY27 on estimates that keep rising, and sentiment is near its lows. KLA showed that a confident 2027 framework is rewarded even in this tape, and a large 14-week FQ1 headline guide could set off a big relief gap. The case for down is also live. This stock has fallen on 5 of its last 7 prints, including beat-and-raises. The five-day squeeze took much of the relief, and margin, opex and tax headwinds give the market an easy reason to sell. I am left near the middle.
approach_notes: P4 ('priced in is a claim to prove') helped: rising FY27 estimates show the peer read-through is in consensus, which stopped a confident long. Unreachable consensus pages (Chartmill 403) left the deciding comparison, FQ1 guide against consensus, unmeasurable. Also noted: a Fox Business quote page stamped 2026-11-19 in a search snippet showed 1-week -14.71% and 1-month -34.38%. Those match the 11-06 close exactly (332.72 against 390.09 on 10-30 and 507.03 on 10-09), so it is not post-print data and not contamination.
